title: Swiss Upper House Approves Proposal to Legalize Marijuana Use

Source: http://www.bloomberg.com/

From Bloomberg

Bern, March 7 (Bloomberg) -- Swiss users of marijuana could soon be consuming the drug without fear of prosecution, after both houses of Switzerland's parliament expressed support for the legalization of all uses of the hemp plant.
(MarijuanaNews note: The phrase " the legalization of all uses of the hemp plant " is relevant to the Alaskan initiative.)
See
NORML Weekly Press Release February 24, 2000

The Swiss government opened a consultation process for a revision of the drugs legislation last August. Today's vote in the upper house of parliament, supporting a regional bid to legalize the use and sale of cannabis, should bring the country one step closer to its legalization, observers said.

Switzerland became notorious for its liberal drug policies, after citizens last June approved a plant to give heroin to long- term addicts. The lower house of parliament approved of a legalization last October.
(MarijuanaNews note: " Notorious? " So much for " objective " journalism! Will Bloomberg become notorious for prohibitionist propaganda?)

" The government probably will propose the new law to parliament this year,'' on complete legalization, said Georg Amstutz, a government spokesman.

Though the two houses expressed support for legalizing marijuana use, they will have to vote again on the issue once the government formulates implementing legislation. The consultation process was closed at the end of last year, and the government now awaits the analysis of its result, Amstutz said.

Today's vote made a law change more likely, as the upper house, the body representing the cantons, is considered the more conservative with a lower share of pro-legalization Social Democrats than the lower house.

Marijuana is consumed by 27 percent of 15- to 35-year olds in Switzerland, according to a government study.
